name: custom matmul matches rectangular forward and backward
test:
import torch
a = torch.randn(2, 3, dtype=torch.double, requires_grad=True)
b = torch.randn(3, 4, dtype=torch.double, requires_grad=True)
assert torch.autograd.gradcheck(matmul, (a, b), eps=1e-6, atol=1e-4)
assert matmul(a, b).shape == (2, 4)

name: broadcast gradients reduce to input shapes
test:
import torch
torch.manual_seed(17)
for a_shape, b_shape in [((1, 2, 3), (4, 3, 5)), ((2, 1, 2, 3), (1, 4, 3, 5)), ((2, 3), (4, 3, 5))]:
    a = torch.randn(a_shape, dtype=torch.double, requires_grad=True)
    b = torch.randn(b_shape, dtype=torch.double, requires_grad=True)
    a_before, b_before = a.detach().clone(), b.detach().clone()
    reference_a = a.detach().clone().requires_grad_()
    reference_b = b.detach().clone().requires_grad_()
    out = matmul(a, b)
    expected = torch.matmul(reference_a, reference_b)
    torch.testing.assert_close(out, expected)
    upstream = torch.randn_like(expected)
    actual_gradients = torch.autograd.grad(out, (a, b), upstream)
    expected_gradients = torch.autograd.grad(expected, (reference_a, reference_b), upstream)
    for actual, expected_gradient, original in zip(actual_gradients, expected_gradients, (a, b)):
        assert actual.shape == original.shape
        assert actual.dtype == original.dtype and actual.device == original.device
        torch.testing.assert_close(actual, expected_gradient)
    assert torch.equal(a, a_before) and torch.equal(b, b_before)

name: manual chain backward agrees with autograd
test:
import torch
torch.manual_seed(3)
for shapes in [[(2, 2), (2, 2), (2, 2)], [(2, 3), (3, 4), (4, 2)], [(2, 3)]]:
    matrices = [torch.randn(shape, dtype=torch.double) for shape in shapes]
    before = [item.clone() for item in matrices]
    values = [item.clone().requires_grad_() for item in matrices]
    expected = values[0]
    for item in values[1:]:
        expected = expected @ item
    torch.testing.assert_close(chain_forward(matrices), expected.detach())
    grad = torch.randn_like(expected)
    manual = chain_backward(matrices, grad)
    expected_gradients = torch.autograd.grad((expected * grad).sum(), values)
    assert len(manual) == len(matrices)
    for actual, expected_gradient, original in zip(manual, expected_gradients, matrices):
        assert actual.shape == original.shape
        assert actual.dtype == original.dtype and actual.device == original.device
        torch.testing.assert_close(actual, expected_gradient)
    assert all(torch.equal(item, old) for item, old in zip(matrices, before))
